# VoiceFleet

> AI voice receptionist for small businesses. Answer calls, take messages, and book appointments 24/7.

Founded 2025. Subscription plans are described on the pricing page. Contact: support@voicefleet.ai.

<!-- Keep in sync with /robots.txt and /ai.txt -->

This index selects 44 pages from 6327 catalog routes. Large collections are capped; the catalog provides the complete route list.

## Core pages

- [VoiceFleet: AI Voice Receptionist & 24/7 Call Answering](https://voicefleet.ai/index.md): VoiceFleet is an AI voice receptionist starting at €99/mo with a 7-day free trial. Answers calls 24/7, books appointments, takes messages, and routes urgent calls. Setup in under 1 hour.
- [AI Receptionist Pricing | From €99/mo + Free Trial | VoiceFleet](https://voicefleet.ai/pricing.md): Compare VoiceFleet AI receptionist plans from €99/mo. See included minutes, 24/7 phone answering, booking capture, setup, annual savings and free trial.
- [Interactive Demo - See AI Phone Calls in Action](https://voicefleet.ai/demo.md): Try VoiceFleet's AI receptionist live. Watch it book appointments, answer questions, and take complete delivery orders in real time.
- [AI Voice Assistant - Available Locations](https://voicefleet.ai/in.md): VoiceFleet AI voice agents are available across Ireland and Europe. Find AI-powered phone automation services in your city.
- [AI Receptionist Alternatives & Comparisons | VoiceFleet](https://voicefleet.ai/compare.md): Compare VoiceFleet with AI receptionist alternatives, answering services, voicemail, call centers, Arini, Ruby and local Ireland providers. See pricing and fit.
- [AI Voice Receptionist for Irish Small Businesses](https://voicefleet.ai/ie.md): AI receptionist for Irish businesses: answer calls, capture appointment requests and hand off urgent enquiries. See the Irish dental call flow and plans from €99/month.
- [24/7 AI Receptionist for US SMBs](https://voicefleet.ai/us.md): VoiceFleet is an AI voice receptionist for US small businesses. Answer calls 24/7, book appointments, take messages, and route urgent calls with US pricing and provisioning.
- [AI Voice Receptionist for Australian Businesses](https://voicefleet.ai/au.md): VoiceFleet is an AI voice receptionist for Australian businesses starting at A$140/mo with a 7-day free trial. Answer calls 24/7, book appointments, take messages, and route urgent calls with local Australian numbers.
- [Recepcionista IA para Negocios en Argentina](https://voicefleet.ai/ar.md): Agentes de voz IA para negocios en Argentina. Atendé llamadas, tomá mensajes y agendá turnos con precios en USD y números locales para el mercado argentino.
- [Recepcionista IA para Empresas en España | VoiceFleet](https://voicefleet.ai/es.md): Recepcionista IA para empresas en España. Automatiza llamadas, captura citas y responde consultas con agentes de voz IA 24/7.

- [AI Phone Answering for Melbourne Vets](https://voicefleet.ai/ai-phone-answering-vet-melbourne.md): Test how VoiceFleet captures routine, urgent-review and after-hours calls for a Melbourne veterinary team.

## Guides and features

- [AI Phone Receptionist for Gyms & Fitness Centers](https://voicefleet.ai/for/gyms.md): Gyms & Fitness Centers teams can use VoiceFleet to answer routine calls, capture caller details, support configured booking workflows, and hand off calls that need a person.

- [VoiceFleet vs Abby Connect: AI Receptionist Comparison](https://voicefleet.ai/blog/2026-03-20-voicefleet-vs-abby-connect.md): VoiceFleet vs Abby Connect — which receptionist service is better for your business? Compare pricing, features, availability, and AI capabilities side by side.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about VoiceFleet

### How do I forward my calls to VoiceFleet?

After signup, you'll get a VoiceFleet number. You then enable call forwarding from your existing number to VoiceFleet. Most providers can be set up in a few minutes.

### Will forwarding my calls create a loop?

No. The call flow is strictly one-directional: your business line forwards to VoiceFleet, and VoiceFleet can escalate to your mobile if needed. Calls never loop back to your business line.

### Do I need to change my phone number?

No. You keep your existing business number. Just enable call forwarding to your VoiceFleet number and your customers continue calling the same number they always have.

### Can it handle accents and names?

Yes. VoiceFleet is built for real-world calls and handles a wide range of accents, names, and pronunciations.

### What happens if the caller needs to speak to a human?

You control escalation. VoiceFleet can transfer to staff, take a detailed message for callback, or flag urgent calls for immediate attention.

### Can it book appointments in my calendar?

Yes. VoiceFleet supports calendar and booking integrations so it can check availability, book appointments, and send confirmations based on your rules.

### How quickly does it answer calls?

VoiceFleet answers quickly and consistently, so callers reach a receptionist experience without long holds.

### Is my data safe and kept in the EU?

VoiceFleet acts as a data processor under its Data Processing Agreement. We offer regional configurations, but some providers or customer-selected integrations may process data outside the EEA. See our Privacy Notice for details.

### Can I customise what the AI says?

Yes. You control greeting, tone, what information to collect, booking rules, and when to escalate to your team.

### What if I'm not happy with the service?

You can cancel anytime. If VoiceFleet isn't a fit, you can stop forwarding calls and close your account.

### How much does an AI receptionist cost?

VoiceFleet AI receptionist plans start at €99/month (Starter, 500 minutes), €299/month (Growth, 1,000 minutes), and €599/month (Pro, 2,000 minutes). Every plan includes a 7-day free trial, 24/7 AI call answering while minutes are available, and a local business phone number. No setup fees or contracts.

### What is an AI voice receptionist?

An AI voice receptionist is software that answers phone calls using conversational AI. Instead of voicemail or hold music, callers speak naturally and the AI handles requests — booking appointments, taking messages, answering FAQs, and routing urgent calls to staff. VoiceFleet is an AI voice receptionist built for small businesses like dental practices, restaurants, and service companies.

### Can an AI receptionist replace a human receptionist?

An AI receptionist handles routine calls like appointment booking, message-taking, and FAQ answers 24/7 without breaks or overtime. It works best as a complement to human staff — answering after-hours calls, handling overflow during busy periods, and freeing front-desk staff for in-person tasks. VoiceFleet escalates complex calls to your team automatically.

### Does VoiceFleet work for restaurants?

Yes. VoiceFleet handles reservation bookings, takeaway orders, menu questions, and opening-hours enquiries for restaurants. It integrates with booking systems like TheFork, OpenTable, and Resy (beta), and sends instant order summaries to your team via SMS or email.

### Does VoiceFleet work for dental practices?

Yes. VoiceFleet books dental appointments, captures patient details and reason for visit, answers common questions about services and insurance, and routes urgent calls to staff. It integrates with calendar systems so patients get confirmed bookings without phone tag.

### How does VoiceFleet compare to Smith.ai?

VoiceFleet is an AI-first voice receptionist starting at €99/month with unlimited calls within your minutes allocation. Smith.ai uses human receptionists with AI assistance, starting at higher price points. VoiceFleet offers 24/7 coverage without per-call fees and calendar integrations. Smith.ai may be better if you need live human agents for complex legal or medical intake.

### Is VoiceFleet available in Ireland?

Yes. VoiceFleet is built for Irish businesses and provides local Irish phone numbers (Dublin and regional). Pricing is in EUR, and the AI handles Irish accents and local business norms. VoiceFleet also serves businesses in Argentina with USD pricing.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about VoiceFleet

### How much does VoiceFleet cost?

VoiceFleet starts at €99/month (Starter) for 500 minutes, €299/month (Growth) for 1,000 minutes, and €599/month (Pro) for 2,000 minutes. No per-call fees, no contracts, and no setup charges. Every plan includes 24/7 AI call answering while minutes are available and a local business phone number.

### How much does an AI receptionist cost compared to hiring a human?

VoiceFleet starts at €99/month with plans that scale by minutes and features. Compared with hiring and scheduling full-time reception coverage, many teams use VoiceFleet to lower fixed costs and improve after-hours call handling.

### Is there a free trial?

Yes. Every plan comes with a 7-day free trial so you can test VoiceFleet with your real business calls before committing. Cancel anytime during the trial.

### What happens if I go over my included minutes?

VoiceFleet does not automatically bill overage. When hard-stop enforcement is active and your verified minute balance reaches zero, new inbound AI calls pause until you buy an extra-minute pack or your plan renews. Billing shows the current enforcement status, and low-balance alerts help you top up in time.

### Can I cancel anytime?

Yes. There are no long-term contracts. You can cancel your subscription at any time and your service continues until the end of the billing period.

### Do you charge per call?

No. VoiceFleet uses prepaid monthly minute allowances rather than per-call fees. You can buy an extra-minute pack when needed, and there is no automatic overage billing.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about VoiceFleet

### How do I forward my calls to VoiceFleet?

After signup, you'll get a VoiceFleet number. You then enable call forwarding from your existing number to VoiceFleet. Most providers can be set up in a few minutes.

### Will forwarding my calls create a loop?

No. The call flow is strictly one-directional: your business line forwards to VoiceFleet, and VoiceFleet can escalate to your mobile if needed. Calls never loop back to your business line.

### Do I need to change my phone number?

No. You keep your existing business number. Just enable call forwarding to your VoiceFleet number and your customers continue calling the same number they always have.

### Can it handle accents and names?

Yes. VoiceFleet is built for real-world calls and handles a wide range of accents, names, and pronunciations.

### What happens if the caller needs to speak to a human?

You control escalation. VoiceFleet can transfer to staff, take a detailed message for callback, or flag urgent calls for immediate attention.

### Can it book appointments in my calendar?

Yes. VoiceFleet supports calendar and booking integrations so it can check availability, book appointments, and send confirmations based on your rules.

### How quickly does it answer calls?

VoiceFleet answers quickly and consistently, so callers reach a receptionist experience without long holds.

### Is my data safe and kept in the EU?

VoiceFleet acts as a data processor under its Data Processing Agreement. We offer regional configurations, but some providers or customer-selected integrations may process data outside the EEA. See our Privacy Notice for details.

### Can I customise what the AI says?

Yes. You control greeting, tone, what information to collect, booking rules, and when to escalate to your team.

### What if I'm not happy with the service?

You can cancel anytime. If VoiceFleet isn't a fit, you can stop forwarding calls and close your account.

### How much does an AI receptionist cost?

VoiceFleet AI receptionist plans start at €99/month (Starter, 500 minutes), €299/month (Growth, 1,000 minutes), and €599/month (Pro, 2,000 minutes). Every plan includes a 7-day free trial, 24/7 AI call answering while minutes are available, and a local business phone number. No setup fees or contracts.

### What is an AI voice receptionist?

An AI voice receptionist is software that answers phone calls using conversational AI. Instead of voicemail or hold music, callers speak naturally and the AI handles requests — booking appointments, taking messages, answering FAQs, and routing urgent calls to staff. VoiceFleet is an AI voice receptionist built for small businesses like dental practices, restaurants, and service companies.

### Can an AI receptionist replace a human receptionist?

An AI receptionist handles routine calls like appointment booking, message-taking, and FAQ answers 24/7 without breaks or overtime. It works best as a complement to human staff — answering after-hours calls, handling overflow during busy periods, and freeing front-desk staff for in-person tasks. VoiceFleet escalates complex calls to your team automatically.

### Does VoiceFleet work for restaurants?

Yes. VoiceFleet handles reservation bookings, takeaway orders, menu questions, and opening-hours enquiries for restaurants. It integrates with booking systems like TheFork, OpenTable, and Resy (beta), and sends instant order summaries to your team via SMS or email.

### Does VoiceFleet work for dental practices?

Yes. VoiceFleet books dental appointments, captures patient details and reason for visit, answers common questions about services and insurance, and routes urgent calls to staff. It integrates with calendar systems so patients get confirmed bookings without phone tag.

### How does VoiceFleet compare to Smith.ai?

VoiceFleet is an AI-first voice receptionist starting at €99/month with unlimited calls within your minutes allocation. Smith.ai uses human receptionists with AI assistance, starting at higher price points. VoiceFleet offers 24/7 coverage without per-call fees and calendar integrations. Smith.ai may be better if you need live human agents for complex legal or medical intake.

### Is VoiceFleet available in Ireland?

Yes. VoiceFleet is built for Irish businesses and provides local Irish phone numbers (Dublin and regional). Pricing is in EUR, and the AI handles Irish accents and local business norms. VoiceFleet also serves businesses in Argentina with USD pricing.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How do I forward my calls to VoiceFleet?

After signup, you'll get a VoiceFleet number. You then enable call forwarding from your existing number to VoiceFleet. Most providers can be set up in a few minutes.

### Will forwarding my calls create a loop?

No. The call flow is strictly one-directional: your business line forwards to VoiceFleet, and VoiceFleet can escalate to your mobile if needed. Calls never loop back to your business line.

### Do I need to change my phone number?

No. You keep your existing business number. Just enable call forwarding to your VoiceFleet number and your customers continue calling the same number they always have.

### Can it handle accents and names?

Yes. VoiceFleet is built for real-world calls and handles a wide range of accents, names, and pronunciations.

### What happens if the caller needs to speak to a human?

You control escalation. VoiceFleet can transfer to staff, take a detailed message for callback, or flag urgent calls for immediate attention.

### Can it book appointments in my calendar?

Yes. VoiceFleet supports calendar and booking integrations so it can check availability, book appointments, and send confirmations based on your rules.

### How quickly does it answer calls?

VoiceFleet answers quickly and consistently, so callers reach a receptionist experience without long holds.

### Is my data safe and kept in the EU?

VoiceFleet supports regional deployment options and privacy-ready configurations. If you have specific Australian privacy or residency requirements, contact us and we'll confirm the right setup for your business.

### Can I customise what the AI says?

Yes. You control greeting, tone, what information to collect, booking rules, and when to escalate to your team.

### What if I'm not happy with the service?

You can cancel anytime. If VoiceFleet isn't a fit, you can stop forwarding calls and close your account.

### What is an AI voice receptionist?

An AI voice receptionist is software that answers phone calls using conversational AI. Instead of voicemail or hold music, callers speak naturally and the AI handles requests — booking appointments, taking messages, answering FAQs, and routing urgent calls to staff. VoiceFleet is an AI voice receptionist built for small businesses like dental practices, restaurants, and service companies.

An AI receptionist handles routine calls like appointment booking, message-taking, and FAQ answers 24/7 without breaks or overtime. VoiceFleet answers your gym's existing number around the clock. It answers questions using the information you give it: membership options and prices, opening hours, your class timetable, facilities and parking.

## VoiceFleet vs Voksha: compare the terms and the workflow

Start with the calls your business needs handled, then compare each supplier's documented limits and a controlled demonstration. A lower subscription price does not establish better value if the plans cover different volumes or tasks. We have not run a controlled product comparison, so this page does not award a performance winner.

**VoiceFleet is our product.** Earlier versions of this article contained unsupported competitor prices and restrictions, claims of superior call handling, clinical-triage promises and an unverified review rating. Those claims have been removed. The information below distinguishes current provider-published terms from questions that still need to be tested.

## What Voksha currently publishes

We checked the [Voksha homepage](https://voksha.com/) on 26 October 2026. Its published plans differ from the previous $49 unlimited-call description on this page:

Voksha planPublished monthly pricePublished allowance and scope
Starter$1415 calls included, then $1 per call; message capture, without appointment bookingPremium$99150 calls included, then $1 per call; adds appointment booking and integrationsEnterpriseFrom $990Custom call volume; request a written quote

Voksha's FAQ says there is no free trial; it offers a free demo call and describes a seven-day money-back guarantee. Confirm the eligibility and current terms before purchasing. Its homepage describes calendar connections on Premium and markets service to businesses in the US, Canada and UK. That does not establish availability of a particular local number or a working integration for your account.

These are Voksha's published statements, not results from our testing. We have not verified its speed, security performance, customer counts or business outcomes. We also do not have evidence for the earlier claims that it cannot serve customers outside the US, has only English support, or lacks a particular industry's workflow.

## VoiceFleet's documented plans

As checked on 26 October 2026, the Ireland/Europe [VoiceFleet pricing page](https://voicefleet.ai/pricing) lists Starter at €99/month with 500 minutes, Growth at €299/month for 1,000 minutes and Pro at €599/month for 2,000 minutes. Confirm the market and currency that apply to your business rather than treating these euro prices as a quote for every country.

PlanIncluded monthly minutesParallel-call capacity
Starter5003Growth1,0005Pro2,00010

These are plan allowances, not unlimited capacity or measured answering performance. The pricing page lists extra-minute packs with no automatic overage; when hard stop is active, a verified zero balance pauses new inbound AI calls until top-up or renewal. It lists a seven-day free trial, no setup fees and no contracts. Check human-transfer access, any add-ons and the supported workflow for your chosen plan.

A call-based allowance and a minute-based allowance are not equivalent. Use your actual call count and durations, peak simultaneous calls, forwarding charges, setup work and any integration fees to compare the total quoted cost. We have not calculated a universal saving or converted currencies to declare one provider cheaper.

## Verify the same requirements with both suppliers

RequirementAsk forVerify in a controlled pilot

Local number and forwardingAvailability for your country and number type, forwarding instructions and chargesInbound calls reach the intended workflow and the fallback still works
Language and call qualitySupported languages and configuration limitsRepresentative names, accents, corrections and background noise
Appointment handlingExact software, permissions and supported read/write actionsA request is distinguished from a saved appointment; inspect the destination record
Human handoffPlan entitlement, routing rules and unavailable-staff behaviorAnswered, unanswered and failed transfers have an agreed next step
Capacity and billingIncluded usage, simultaneous-call limits and exhausted-allowance behaviorPeak-load and low-balance cases produce the expected result

## What are you buying?

A live answering service uses people to handle calls under an agreed service scope. An AI answering service uses software configured with business information and handling instructions. For either option, establish which tasks are included, which require access to another system, and which must go to your team.

Do not treat “appointment handling” as a single capability. Taking a preferred time and callback number is different from checking availability and creating a confirmed booking. Ask the provider to show the exact workflow with your account's supported integration. A spoken confirmation alone is not proof of a completed booking.

## Compare the actual workload, not a headline price

Ask each provider for a written quote using the same expected call volume, average duration, operating hours and escalation requirements. Check whether usage is counted in calls, minutes or another unit. Confirm how transfers, short calls, spam, holidays, extra usage and telephone forwarding are charged.

| Coverage | Contracted hours, exclusions and the fallback when answering is unavailable |
| Capacity | Simultaneous-call limit and what happens above that limit |
| Price | Currency, taxes, included usage, extra usage and any forwarding charges |
| Task completion | A demonstration of the requested action in the connected system |
| Human help | Transfer entitlement, destination availability and failed-transfer handling |
| Privacy | Recording settings, retention, subprocessors, processing locations and contractual terms |

## When to evaluate human answering, AI or a combined workflow

Consider human-led handling when your requirements involve substantial discretion, distressed callers, negotiation or callers who specifically want a person. Confirm that the proposed live service actually includes those tasks; an operator may also be limited to a script or message-taking.

## A practical acceptance check before changing routing

Use synthetic caller details and a controlled test setup. The checklist below is an unperformed test plan, not evidence that VoiceFleet or another provider has passed it.

1. **Approved information:** ask a routine question, then an unknown question. Check that the answer stays within the business's approved information and that uncertainty is handled appropriately.
2. **Corrections:** change a name, date or requested time during the call. Inspect the resulting message or test booking instead of relying only on what was said.
3. **Escalation:** ask for a person. Test both an available destination and an unavailable one, including the agreed callback alternative.
4. **Capacity and continuity:** agree a safe test of concurrent calls, unavailable integrations and the zero-balance policy. Do not assume the service can accept unlimited traffic.
5. **Privacy and records:** confirm what is recorded, who can access it and when it is deleted. Avoid real customer or patient information in the test.
6. **Decision:** record pass, fail and untested outcomes. Keep staff involved until the agreed requirements are met; a demo alone does not prove production reliability.

There is no universal result in this guide. Evaluate the specific task, caller needs, failure handling and evidence from a controlled pilot. We have not established that callers cannot distinguish AI from people or that either option is always faster or more accurate.

### How much does a live answering service cost?

Obtain a current quote for your usage and scope. We have removed the earlier competitor price table because its figures and effective per-call calculations were not supported by current verified sources. Compare equivalent currencies and included services before drawing a cost conclusion.

No zero-risk promise is supported. Confirm forwarding and rollback, retain a working fallback and review actual results before expanding the scope. Keeping two subscriptions does not by itself prove that calls will reach the intended destination.

### Can an AI receptionist book appointments or transfer calls?

That depends on the product, plan, integration and configuration. Capturing an appointment request is not the same as completing a booking.

VoiceFleet is our product. This guide is a proposed evaluation method, not results of a side-by-side product test. We do not have verified evidence here for an industry-wide Irish price range, a guaranteed response time, accent-recognition accuracy or customer revenue and booking improvements.

## What are you comparing?

A live answering service uses people to handle calls on your behalf. An AI receptionist uses software to conduct a conversation within its configured scope. Either service needs agreed instructions for questions it cannot answer and a clear route to a responsible person.

Do not assume that every human service only takes messages, or that every AI service can complete a booking. Ask each supplier to demonstrate the exact workflow you intend to buy. A caller being told an appointment is booked is not proof that the correct appointment exists in the destination calendar.

## Compare the same call-handling requirements

| Requirement | Ask the live answering supplier | Ask the AI supplier |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage | Which hours, holidays and overflow arrangements are included? | Which hours and routing conditions are configured, and what happens during an outage? |
| Simultaneous calls | How does the service handle demand above staffed capacity? | What is the plan's parallel-call limit and what happens when it is reached? |
| Booking | Can the operator use the exact system and permissions you require? | Can the configured workflow complete and verify the exact action in that system? |
| Exceptions | Which requests must be passed back to your team? | How are uncertain answers and requests outside the approved scope handled? |
| Languages and accents | Can you evaluate the people or coverage offered for your callers? | Can you test representative pronunciation, names and noisy conditions? |
| Cost | What is included, how is usage measured and what costs extra? | What is included, how is usage measured and what happens when the balance runs out? |
| Privacy | What are the processing terms, recording rules and access controls? | What are the processing terms, recording rules and access controls? |

These are questions for evaluation, not assertions that either supplier has passed them.

## Compare quotes without invented averages

Use your own recent call records to estimate call count, connected minutes, peak concurrency and the proportion needing human follow-up. Keep customer details out of any initial evaluation material. Request a quote for that same workload from each supplier.

Ask for setup costs, included usage, additional usage, out-of-hours handling, transfers, booking work and cancellation terms in writing. A quoted price per call is not directly comparable with a price per connected minute unless the workload assumptions are explicit. Include the time your team still spends resolving messages or correcting mistakes.

As checked on 23 October 2026, the [VoiceFleet pricing page](https://voicefleet.ai/pricing) lists:

The same page lists parallel-call capacities of 3, 5 and 10 respectively. It also states that, when hard stop is active, a verified zero balance pauses new inbound AI calls until top-up or renewal. These are published plan terms, not unlimited-call promises or measurements of your likely bill. Check current pricing and the applicable terms before choosing a plan.

We do not provide a competing supplier's price or an expected savings percentage here without a current, comparable quote. Do not treat removed historical figures as a benchmark.

## When human handling may be important

Start with the calls that require judgement, sensitivity or responsibility. Define which conversations must reach a trained member of your team rather than asking any answering service to improvise. For legal, clinical or other sensitive enquiries, agree the permitted scope and escalation process with the person responsible for those services.

Do not infer confidentiality or regulatory suitability from whether a caller speaks to a person or software. Review the contract and actual data flow. VoiceFleet's [Privacy Notice](https://voicefleet.ai/privacy) and [Data Processing Agreement](https://voicefleet.ai/dpa) describe its processing arrangements. Some providers or customer-selected integrations may process data outside the EEA. This is not a blanket compliance or EU-only residency guarantee.

## A practical trial before changing your routing

Use synthetic calls and a test destination approved for the trial. Do not send real patient or client information merely to see whether a demo works. Agree the pass conditions before testing.

1. **Routine enquiry:** ask a question covered by your approved information. Check that the response is accurate and does not invent a policy or price.
2. **Unknown question:** ask something outside that information. Check the actual fallback rather than accepting a confident answer.
3. **Booking request:** if booking is in scope, request a slot and then inspect the destination calendar for the correct date, time, contact and service. Test an unavailable slot and a correction separately.
4. **Human request:** ask to speak to a person. Check what happens when the intended recipient answers and when nobody is available.
5. **Peak demand:** evaluate the agreed simultaneous-call limit and the handling of an additional call, using a controlled test arrangement.
6. **Speech and noise:** try representative names, pronunciation and background noise. Record errors; do not substitute an unsupported accuracy percentage.
7. **Failure conditions:** agree how unavailable integrations, insufficient balance and outages will be handled, and verify the arrangements that can safely be tested.

These checks have not been performed for the reader's business. A successful demo of one scenario does not establish all integrations, every accent or every failure path.

## Could a hybrid arrangement work?

A limited-scope trial can help you decide whether selected routine or overflow calls belong with an AI service while other calls remain with people. Confirm that your phone routing and both suppliers support the proposed arrangement before changing anything.

Keep an explicit fallback and a way to restore the previous routing. There is no universal two-week migration schedule or guaranteed disruption-free switch. Expand only after the agreed checks and a review of actual call outcomes.

## How to judge the result

Compare similar periods and record the workload, calls that needed correction, completed actions confirmed in the destination system, human follow-up and total cost. Separate a captured booking request from a confirmed appointment. Do not present a rise in revenue or bookings as caused by the answering service without evidence addressing other changes.

If the trial does not meet the requirements, narrow its scope, change the configuration or retain the existing arrangement. Neither technology is the right choice for every Irish business.

## VoiceFleet vs 8x8: A Detailed Comparison

### Pricing

8x8 operates a fully quote-based pricing model — they no longer list costs publicly, meaning you must engage a sales representative before knowing what you will pay [1](https://www.cloudtalk.io/blog/8x8-pricing/). Industry estimates place standard unified communications plans at **$24–$44/user/month** billed annually, with full omnichannel contact centre access reaching **$140/user/month** before add-ons. One-off setup fees range from **$1,000 to $25,000+**, and enterprise deployments typically cost **$40,000–$55,000 per year** after negotiation. Annual billing saves approximately 15–23% compared to monthly pricing.

VoiceFleet Starter is A$140/month for 500 minutes, Growth is A$424/month for 1,000 minutes, and Pro is A$851/month for 2,000 minutes. No setup fees. No contracts.

### What You Are Actually Buying

These are fundamentally different products that serve different needs:

- **8x8** is a **UCaaS/CCaaS platform** — it gives your human team a suite of communication tools: business VoIP, video conferencing (up to 500 participants), team messaging, and a contact centre console. Your staff still answers calls; 8x8 equips them to do so more efficiently.
- **VoiceFleet** is an **AI voice agent** — it *replaces* the human receptionist entirely. It answers every inbound call autonomously, handles FAQs, books appointments, and qualifies leads around the clock with no staff required.

### AI Capabilities

8x8's AI features are analytics-focused: call transcription, speech analytics, live coaching for agents, and workforce management scheduling now bundled into every contact centre seat at no extra cost [2](https://softabase.com/software/voip/8x8). These are powerful tools for contact centre managers overseeing human teams, but they augment agents rather than replacing them.

VoiceFleet's AI is the product itself. Research shows AI voice agents handle calls at roughly **$0.05–$0.40 per interaction**, compared to **$7–$12 per call** for human agents — a cost reduction of **up to 95%** [3](https://www.ringly.io/blog/voice-ai-statistics-2026). Gartner forecasts **$80 billion in contact centre labour savings** driven by conversational AI by 2026 [6](https://agentmarketcap.ai/blog/2026/04/05/voice-ai-agents-kill-the-call-center), and Forrester Consulting reports a **3-year ROI of up to 391%** for organisations adopting voice AI at scale [3](https://www.ringly.io/blog/voice-ai-statistics-2026).

### Reliability and Customer Experience

8x8 markets a **99.999% uptime SLA** and has earned a strong reputation for reliability in many markets. However, recent customer reviews raise concerns about dropped calls, mobile app instability following software updates, and — most critically — support that has migrated to an **AI-only model**, making it very difficult to reach a human representative when issues arise [4](https://getvoip.com/reviews/8x8-inc/). Some customers report spending multiple days attempting to contact support after service disruptions.

### Contract and Cancellation

This is an area where 8x8 has attracted significant criticism in 2025–2026. Multiple customers report **early termination fees of $1,500–$1,800+** and describe difficulty cancelling services or identifying contract expiry dates [5](https://www.techmode.com/8x8-alternatives-2026-reviews-problems/). VoiceFleet operates without lock-in contracts, and customers can adjust or cancel their plan at any time.

### Global Reach

8x8 genuinely leads here: **local phone numbers in 100+ countries** and unlimited calling to **48 countries** makes it one of the most globally capable UCaaS providers available [2](https://softabase.com/software/voip/8x8). For multinational enterprises with distributed teams, this is a compelling advantage VoiceFleet does not currently match. ### Who Each Product Is Built For

Five9 is an enterprise-grade cloud contact centre platform designed for organisations running structured, high-volume call centre operations. Its feature set — omnichannel routing, workforce management, real-time analytics, and deep CRM integrations — is powerful and genuinely impressive. But it is architected for teams of 50+ agents, not for a dental practice that needs calls answered after hours.

VoiceFleet is an AI voice agent platform built for SMBs across Ireland and Europe. It answers every inbound call automatically, books appointments, handles FAQs, qualifies leads, and integrates with your existing calendar — with no human agents, no IT department, and no long-term commitment required.

---

### Pricing: The Starkest Difference

Five9 publishes tiered per-seat pricing starting at **$119 per user/month** for the Digital plan (digital channels only, no voice) and **$159 per user/month** for the Core plan (voice + digital channels). These prices apply on a **36-month contract** with a **minimum of 50 concurrent seats**. [1](https://www.nextiva.com/blog/five9-pricing.html)

This means the bare minimum spend on Five9 is approximately **$5,950–$7,950/month** (~€5,500–€7,350/month at current rates) — before any professional services fees for implementation, which typically run 4–12 weeks and can extend to 6 months. [2](https://www.getnextphone.com/blog/five9-integration)

Higher tiers — Premium ($169/user/month), Optimum ($199/user/month), and Ultimate ($229/user/month) — add workforce management, AI analytics, and advanced features, but pricing requires custom quotes for most enterprise needs. [1](https://www.nextiva.com/blog/five9-pricing.html)

VoiceFleet Starter is €99/month for 500 minutes, Growth is €299/month for 1,000 minutes, and Pro is €599/month for 2,000 minutes.

No per-seat fees. No minimum user count. No multi-year contracts required.

### Features: Enterprise Power vs SMB Simplicity

Five9's **Intelligent Virtual Agent (IVA)** is a genuine AI capability — supporting over 130 languages, 25 synthetic voice avatars, and generative AI blended with traditional NLP. In November 2024, Five9 launched next-generation AI Agents with personalised context transfer and a flexible 'dial-of-trust' for balancing scripted and generative responses. These are impressive capabilities for enterprise deployments. [4](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20241113793597/en/Five9-Unveils-AI-Agents-to-Redefine-Hyper-Personalized-Self-Service-CX)

However, customer reviews on Capterra and Nextiva highlight consistent pain points: the system **crashes frequently during live interactions**, audio quality can degrade, dropped calls are reported, and the backend is described as 'powerful but dense' — typically requiring a dedicated administrator. [3](https://www.nextiva.com/blog/five9-reviews.html)

VoiceFleet's AI voice agents are designed to work out of the box: calendar integration, appointment booking, FAQ handling, and call qualification are configured without technical expertise. Test response quality, availability and escalation with your own call scenarios; error-free handling and uninterrupted service are not guaranteed.

---

### Setup and Implementation

Five9 implementations typically take **4 to 12 weeks** for standard deployments and can take **3 to 6 months** for complex integrations with enterprise CRMs. [2](https://www.getnextphone.com/blog/five9-integration) Dedicated IT resources are required for API configuration, workflow setup, user permissions, number migration, and agent training.

VoiceFleet is live in **minutes**. No IT department. No professional services engagement. No weeks of onboarding.

---

### The AI Opportunity: Why This Matters Now

Gartner predicts that conversational AI will reduce contact centre agent labour costs by **$80 billion by 2026**, with 1 in 10 agent interactions automated. [5](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2022-08-31-gartner-predicts-conversational-ai-will-reduce-contac) Labour expenses represent up to 95% of contact centre costs, and AI voice agents now cost $0.30–$0.50 per call compared to $6–$7.68 for a human agent interaction — a saving of 93–95%. For Irish SMBs, the question is not whether to adopt AI voice technology — it is which platform fits your scale. Five9 brings that technology wrapped in enterprise complexity and cost. VoiceFleet brings it wrapped in a €99/month subscription.

### Verdict

If you are running an enterprise contact centre with 50+ agents, complex omnichannel needs, and a dedicated IT team, Five9 is a legitimate and capable solution worth evaluating. If you are a business owner in Ireland who wants every call answered professionally without hiring a receptionist or signing a 36-month enterprise contract, VoiceFleet is the clear choice.

# Privacy Notice

## 1. Who we are and when this notice applies

VoiceFleet ("VoiceFleet", "we", or "us") operates the VoiceFleet business voice-assistant service from Ireland. Our public service address is Dublin, Ireland. You can contact us at [support@voicefleet.ai](mailto:support@voicefleet.ai).

This notice covers visitors to our websites, account holders and team members, people who communicate with us, callers who interact with a customer's VoiceFleet assistant, and business contacts shown in our public directory.

VoiceFleet is a controller for website, account, billing, security, support, marketing, and directory data. For call content, recordings, transcripts, booking details, and connected business systems, the VoiceFleet customer normally decides why and how the data is used and is the controller; VoiceFleet acts as its processor under our [Data Processing Agreement](https://voicefleet.ai/dpa). Contact the relevant business first if your request concerns a call you made to that business.

## 2. Personal data we process and where it comes from

- Account and business details, such as name, work email, organisation, role, settings, and authentication identifiers.
- Billing and subscription records. Stripe processes complete payment-card details; VoiceFleet receives transaction and limited card metadata.
- Technical and security data, including IP address, device/browser information, login and audit events, region, referral source, and service usage.
- Call data, including caller and called numbers, time, duration, recording, transcript, summary, messages, booking details, and customer-configured instructions.
- Support, demo, and sales communications, including microphone audio and transcripts when you choose to use a voice demo.
- Voice samples, generated voice identifiers, and proof of authority when voice cloning is used.
- Connected-service data and OAuth tokens for calendar, booking, CRM, and communication integrations you enable.
- Public business-directory information, such as business name, public contact details, category, website, and location.

We receive data directly from account users and callers, automatically from devices and the service, from a customer that configures VoiceFleet, from connected providers, and from public business websites or directories. We do not intentionally require callers to provide sensitive data. Customers using VoiceFleet for regulated or special-category data must first satisfy the requirements in the Terms and DPA.

## 3. Why we use data and our legal bases

- **Provide the service and manage accounts:** performance of our contract and steps requested before entering it.
- **Process calls, bookings, and integrations for customers:** the customer's documented instructions under the DPA.
- **Billing, accounting, and legal records:** contract and legal obligations.
- **Security, abuse prevention, troubleshooting, and service reliability:** our legitimate interests in protecting and operating VoiceFleet.
- **Product improvement and anonymous aggregate measurement:** our legitimate interests, with data minimisation and opt-out controls.
- **Requested communications and support:** contract, legitimate interests, or consent depending on the message.
- **Optional marketing:** consent where required; you may unsubscribe at any time.
- **Public business directory:** legitimate interests in providing accurate business discovery, balanced against the rights of listed contacts.
- **Compliance, claims, and authorities:** legal obligations and legitimate interests in establishing or defending legal claims.

Where consent is the basis, you may withdraw it without affecting earlier processing. If providing data is required for an account or requested feature and you do not provide it, we may be unable to supply that feature.

## 4. Calls, AI, recording, and transcription

VoiceFleet adds a spoken notice that the caller is interacting with an AI assistant and that the call may be recorded and transcribed. A customer may need to provide further information or obtain consent depending on its purpose and applicable law. The customer is responsible for choosing and documenting its lawful basis, publishing its own caller notice, and configuring the service lawfully. If consent is required, recording must not continue without valid consent.

## 5. Google user data

If you connect Google Calendar, we access calendar account metadata, calendar identifiers and names, time zones, free/busy availability, relevant event information, appointment details created or updated through VoiceFleet, and OAuth access or refresh tokens needed to keep the integration connected.

We use this data only to provide the calendar features you request: choosing a calendar, checking availability, creating, updating or cancelling appointments, sending invitations or updates, and maintaining the connection. Data may be visible to authorised VoiceFleet account users, Google Calendar, appointment attendees, and subprocessors strictly as needed to provide those functions or comply with law.

We do not sell Google user data, use it for advertising, or use it to train general-purpose AI models. OAuth tokens are not shared with voice or language-model providers. Information sent to AI services is limited to what is needed for the scheduling request. VoiceFleet's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including its Limited Use requirements.

You can disconnect Google Calendar in VoiceFleet or your Google Account. We then delete stored OAuth tokens promptly. Existing calendar events remain in the relevant calendars until their owners delete them.

## 6. Who receives data

We disclose data only as needed to:

- VoiceFleet personnel and authorised users of the relevant customer workspace.
- Infrastructure, database, authentication, telephony, speech-to-text, voice, AI, email, monitoring, payment, and support providers.
- Google, Microsoft, calendar, booking, CRM, and other integrations selected by the customer.
- Professional advisers, insurers, auditors, potential business successors, courts, regulators, or law enforcement where lawfully necessary.

The current core provider list and purposes appear in the [DPA subprocessor schedule](https://voicefleet.ai/dpa#subprocessors). We do not sell personal data.

## 7. International transfers

We offer regional configurations, but some providers or customer-selected integrations may process data outside the EEA. Where required, we use an adequacy decision, the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses, the UK addendum, or another lawful safeguard. Contact us for information about the safeguard relevant to your data.

## 8. Retention

- **Call recordings:** 30 days, after which the provider copy and VoiceFleet recording link are deleted.
- **Call logs, transcripts, summaries, and bookings:** while the customer account is active and normally for up to 30 days after account closure, unless the customer deletes them earlier or law requires longer.
- **Account, support, and configuration data:** while the account is active and normally for up to 30 days after closure.
- **OAuth tokens:** until the integration is disconnected, access is revoked, or the account is deleted.
- **Voice samples and clones:** until the user deletes the clone or the account closes, subject to provider deletion cycles.
- **Invoices, payments, contracts, and acceptance evidence:** up to six years after the relevant transaction or end of the relationship where needed for Irish tax, accounting, or legal claims.
- **Security logs:** normally up to 12 months unless needed to investigate an incident.
- **Directory information:** while it remains publicly available and relevant, subject to correction or objection.

Restricted backup copies may remain until overwritten under provider backup cycles. We isolate them from ordinary use and delete or anonymise data when no longer needed.

## 9. Cookies and analytics

### Partner referral supplement · 16 September 2026

If you arrive through a partner link, we ask before saving an optional referral record in your browser. The choice shows its expiry period. If you sign up within that period, we record the referring partner against your account to calculate commissions. Partners see signup counts, commission amounts, and payout records; they do not receive your contact details or call data. You can clear a saved referral below before signing up. We also process partner contact details and agreed commercial terms to administer the program.

VoiceFleet uses essential browser storage for authentication, security, preferences, and requested service functions. We do not load Google Analytics. We use a self-hosted Umami installation for cookieless, aggregate site measurement. It does not set analytics cookies or identify visitors across websites; search strings and URL fragments are excluded, apart from campaign labels (such as utm\_source) and whether an ad click brought you here, and browser Do Not Track is respected.

### Site measurement supplement · 11 November 2026

From this date the campaign labels and ad-click marker described above are kept with a page view. On our home, pricing, demo, and sign-up pages, the same Umami installation also records a sample of visits: page layout, scrolling, pointer movement, and clicks, which we use to find and fix usability problems. Page text and anything typed into a form are masked in your browser before a recording is sent, the content of other pages is never recorded, recordings are deleted after 30 days, and browsers that send Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control are not recorded.

## 10. Security

We use measures appropriate to the service, including encrypted transport, provider encryption at rest, access controls, tenant separation, secrets management, monitoring, backups, and retention controls. No online system is completely secure. Customers must protect their credentials and configure access appropriately.

## 11. Your rights

Subject to applicable law, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, or portability of your personal data; object to processing based on legitimate interests or direct marketing; and withdraw consent. You may also complain to the [Irish Data Protection Commission](https://www.dataprotection.ie/) or your local supervisory authority. We do not use account or caller data to make solely automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects.

Email [support@voicefleet.ai](mailto:support@voicefleet.ai). We may verify your identity. For customer-controlled call data, we will normally refer the request to or assist the relevant customer.

## 12. Changes and contact

We will post material changes here and, where appropriate, notify account administrators. Questions can be sent to [support@voicefleet.ai](mailto:support@voicefleet.ai) or by post to Dublin, Ireland.
